options: a:Railroad crossings ahead.,b:No passing zones.,c:School zones.,d:Stop signs ahead.
note: Crossbuck signs indicate a railroad crossing; drivers must yield to trains and not try to outrun them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you must yield to traffic when merging and cannot merge safely, does yield also require stopping?
options: a:Only for commercial vehicles.,b:False — yield never requires stopping.,c:True — yield can require stopping if you cannot merge safely.,d:Only during daylight hours.
note: If you cannot safely merge into traffic you must stop and yield until it is safe to merge.

question: If another driver cuts you off, the safest response is to:
options: a:Flash high beams and tailgate them.,b:Let it go and continue driving safely.,c:Pull next to them and argue.,d:Brake-check them immediately.
note: Avoid road rage by remaining calm and continuing to drive defensively.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What do speed limit signs legally indicate?
options: a:The maximum or minimum speed that is legally allowed to be driven,b:The speed drivers should drive in heavy traffic,c:Only a suggested speed
note: Speed limit signs indicate the maximum and/or minimum legal speeds for a roadway under ideal conditions; reduce speed when conditions are hazardous.

question: If you encounter an aggressive driver, what should you do?
options: a:Cut them off to slow them down,b:Retaliate aggressively,c:Avoid eye contact,d:Call them names
note: Stay calm, give distance, avoid confrontation, and let the aggressive driver pass to reduce risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see a steady yellow traffic light as you approach an intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Always speed up to beat the light.,b:Make a U-turn immediately.,c:Stop before entering the intersection if it is safe to do so.,d:Ignore it and proceed at the same speed.
note: A steady yellow light warns the green phase is ending; stop if you can do so safely.

question: When should you use your turn signals?
options: a:Any time you change lanes, pull into or out of parking, or enter traffic from an alley.,b:Only when other vehicles are present.,c:Only during daylight hours.,d:Never when turning right.
note: Always signal before turning, changing lanes, or pulling into/from traffic so others know your intentions.

question: If you become stranded in a snowstorm, what is the best course of action?
options: a:Lie down in the vehicle and sleep.,b:Stay inside your vehicle and wait for help.,c:Leave the vehicle to seek help immediately.,d:Walk into the road to flag down cars.
note: Staying in your car increases the chance of being located and reduces exposure to severe weather.

question: Which of the following parking restrictions is illegal in Virginia?
options: a:Parking in a parking lot,b:Parking on private property with permission,c:Parking within 15 feet of a fire hydrant
note: It is illegal to park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant. Other prohibited parking locations include within 20 feet of an intersection and within 50 feet of a railroad crossing.

question: Guide signs that give directional and mileage information are what color?
options: a:Yellow,b:Red,c:Green
note: Guide or destination signs have green backgrounds and provide directional and mileage information to help drivers reach destinations.

question: Which factors affect braking distance?
options: a:All of the above,b:Condition of brakes and tires,c:Vehicle speed,d:Pavement condition
note: Braking distance depends on speed, brakes and tires, roadway conditions, vehicle weight, and visibility.

question: Children under what age must be secured in an approved child safety seat in Virginia?
options: a:Five,b:Six,c:Eight
note: All children under age eight must be properly secured in an appropriate child safety or booster seat when riding in vehicles manufactured after January 1, 1968, unless exempted by law.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you enter a freeway from an entrance ramp?
options: a:Signal,b:Signal and enter the freeway; freeway traffic must yield.,c:Drive slowly so you can check traffic.
note: Use the acceleration lane to match the speed of traffic, signal, yield to freeway vehicles, and merge when safe.

question: What does a flashing red light on a traffic signal mean?
options: a:Proceed with caution,b:The signal is broken.,c:The same as a stop sign.,d:You do not have to stop.
note: A flashing red light means stop, yield to others, and proceed only when it is safe, just like a stop sign.

question: When must you stop at a railroad crossing?
options: a:When directed to do so by a flagger or a stop sign or when warning devices are active.,b:Only if a train is visible.,c:You never have to stop.
note: You must stop at railroad crossings when directed by a flagger or stop sign and when flashing signals or gates indicate a train is approaching.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is the posted maximum speed limit the fastest you are allowed to drive in all conditions?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Posted speed limits are the maximum under ideal conditions; you must slow down when road, weather, or visibility conditions require it.

question: Why should you avoid following other vehicles too closely?
options: a:You won't see the car's color.,b:You may not have time to stop if they slow or stop suddenly.,c:You may not hear their stereo.,d:It makes lane changes easier
note: Following too closely reduces your reaction time and ability to stop safely if the vehicle ahead slows or stops abruptly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which vehicles are HOV lanes not intended for?
options: a:High-occupancy vehicles.,b:Tractor-trailers.,c:Motorcycles,d:Carpools.
note: High-occupancy vehicle lanes are reserved for buses, carpools, motorcycles, and certain qualifying vehicles; large tractor-trailers are not allowed.

question: What danger can a leaking exhaust system create for vehicle occupants?
options: a:Improved engine performance.,b:Lower fuel efficiency only.,c:Excessive engine oil consumption.,d:Exposure to carbon monoxide that can cause drowsiness or death.
note: A leaky exhaust can introduce toxic fumes, including carbon monoxide, into the cabin and cause drowsiness or worse.

question: When should you stop at an accident scene?
options: a:Stop and block the road to prevent others from passing.,b:Stop only to take photos.,c:Only if you are involved or emergency help has not yet arrived.,d:Always stop and gather a crowd.
note: Do not stop at accident scenes out of curiosity; only stop if required to render aid or if you are involved.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is something you should NOT do when changing lanes?
options: a:Signal to show your intention,b:Fail to check your mirrors and blind spot,c:Check for other drivers moving into the same lane
note: Before changing lanes you should check mirrors, signal your intentions, and glance over your shoulder to check blind spots; failing to do so is unsafe.

question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is approaching, what must you do?
options: a:Speed up to get out of the way,b:Stop immediately in your lane to block traffic,c:Make every effort to give the emergency vehicle a clear path of travel
note: When an emergency vehicle with lights/siren is approaching, safely pull to the side and stop if necessary to allow it to pass.

question: Which of the following is commonly used to direct drivers into the proper lanes for turning?
options: a:Flashing red lights.,b:White lines on the road edge.,c:Arrow lane markings.
note: Arrows painted on pavement and overhead direct drivers into the correct lane for turning or going straight.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Upon seeing an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must:
options: a:Slow down and continue without stopping.,b:Keep driving in your lane.,c:Pull to the right curb and stop.
note: When an emergency vehicle is approaching with lights or siren, pull over to the curb or side of the road and stop to allow it to pass.

question: Compared to smaller cars, truck and bus blind spots are:
options: a:Much larger,b:About the same size,c:Much smaller
note: Large vehicles have much larger blind spots, and drivers of smaller vehicles should avoid lingering in these areas where the truck driver cannot see them.

question: Which has priority over the others at an intersection?
options: a:A steady red light,b:A flashing yellow light,c:A stop sign,d:A police officer directing traffic
note: An authorized officer directing traffic takes precedence over traffic signals, signs, and pavement markings.

question: At a four-way intersection where all directions have stop signs and two drivers arrive simultaneously, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on the right,b:One driver may continue without stopping,c:The driver on the left
note: When two drivers arrive at the same time at a four-way stop, yield to the vehicle on your right and proceed only when safe.

question: How can stress affect your driving?
options: a:It can lower your ability to focus on driving.,b:It decreases your chances of an accident.,c:It causes you to fall asleep at the wheel.,d:It always improves reaction time
note: Emotional stress reduces concentration and can impair your ability to drive safely; consider delaying driving if emotionally upset.

question: Is it illegal for a car to share a single lane with a motorcycle?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Motorcycles are entitled to the full width of a traffic lane and cars must not try to share the lane with a motorcycle.

question: If you turn onto a two-lane road marked with a broken yellow centerline, what does that tell you?
options: a:It is a one-way road.,b:The road is closed for repairs.,c:You must stop before entering.,d:Traffic on that road moves in both directions (two-way road).
note: A broken yellow centerline separates opposing traffic, indicating a two-way road.
